summary: Session 1 profiles slow reads (JSONStorage re-parses the file on every read); the user mentions in passing that an mtime-based cache was tried before and had to be removed, because the db sits on NFS with 1-second mtime resolution and same-second writes by the importer were missed. The last session asks for a read cache that still sees other processes' writes. The natural fix is a stat (mtime/size) check; the hidden test simulates a same-second, same-size write by another process.

turns: Reads are slow on our big db files (~40MB). I think JSONStorage re-parses the whole file on every query, but I'd like numbers. Can you add a small benchmark script under scripts/ that generates a big db and times db.all() and a search, and tell me where the time goes?

Thanks, that matches what I expected. One thing for when we fix it: we had an mtime-based cache last year and had to rip it out. The db files live on an NFS share where mtime only has 1-second resolution, so when the importer wrote within the same second we kept serving stale data. Commit the benchmark script for now, I'll think about the approach.

Let's continue with the read performance work: repeated reads shouldn't re-parse the JSON when the file hasn't changed. The importer process writes to the same file, so its changes still need to show up.

facts.text: Don't decide whether the file changed from its mtime (or other stat data): on the NFS share mtime has 1-second resolution, and an mtime-based cache already served stale data after same-second writes by the importer.
